assessments.reasoning: The sole supporting dependency is spdx_detail, freshly retrieved with HTTP 200 from the SPDX-generated data at commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. The complete 13,320-byte capture had observed SHA-256 98a8503dff3c3efe9629a5d11df3dfa6c855606b153f8cc0ee48bc701340330d. The separately fetched claim record at ab83a4adb7ae90d20dbf15e22ccc4ed2e2645902 matched the requested record digest. The release index, legacy XML, and GCC publisher copy served as comparison controls. The release index and detail share the same generated SPDX commit, and the SPDX text and GCC copy describe the same FSF instrument.

challenge.method: Compared the detail with the pinned release label and row, inspected spdx_legacy [99,509) for a competing deprecated identifier, and checked the exception title, edition, and date against the pinned GCC publisher copy.
challenge.results: The release index agreed with the detail. The legacy XML marks GPL-3.0-with-GCC-exception deprecated in 2.0rc2 and cites GCC-exception-3.1 within replacement expressions. The publisher copy confirmed the named edition and date. The controls disclosed no contradiction to the scoped correspondence.

limitations: The finding is limited to documentary identifier correspondence at the pinned SPDX release. Formal SPDX template matching and any license assignment to a particular file require separate evidence.
The inspected representations differ in line wrapping and in the general-information line. The GNU locator was verified as an entry field.
Migration rules for deprecated combined IDs fall outside the claim.
